creator: Alexander Terp
description:
GitHub issue #2 part 5 (0.15.0): `muster pane wait --pane <name>` is refused when it goes through a window, though every other `--pane` takes a name. With a pane made by `pane new --name pw-probe-1`, `muster pane wait --pane pw-probe-1 --until idle` exited 1:

```
no daemon this window is following holds a pane called pw-probe-1, so there is nothing to watch. Either it closed, or the name came from an older window
```

It failed both while the pane was hidden and after `pane show` put it in a tab. The same wait by id worked, the same wait by name with `--no-window` worked, and `pane read --pane pw-probe-1` and `msg post --to pw-probe-1` both resolved the name. The 0.15 release notes say every `--pane` takes a name.

`pane wait` goes over the window's watch stream (`follow` in `crates/muster-seam/src/command.rs`, then `watch_panes` in `handler.rs`). That path never runs `session::address_panes`, which `handler::handle` runs for every other request, so a name is never turned into an id for a wait. Add a test that waits on a pane by name through a window, hidden and shown.

Two tooling-feedback reports hit the same thing on 0.15.0, one with names set by Claude Code's `/rename` that contain spaces and emoji (`🤖 1 session`), so check those resolve too once the lookup is in. The same report found that `$MUSTER_PANE_NAME` keeps the old name after a rename; `docs/cli/limits.md` already says so, so that part is expected.
title: pane wait --pane <name> is refused through a window
